chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Al-Husayn Sa'eed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) declared forbidden from Medina that which is from Dhubab to Al-Aqim, Al-Areedh, and Al-Naqb from the side of Mecca. Ibn Maskan said in his narration: And in another narration: From As-Sur to Ath-Thaniyyah.

key_terms.الثَّنِيَّة: Ath-Thaniyyah (a narrow mountain pass marking a boundary)
key_terms.الصُّور: As-Sur (a place name marking a boundary)
key_terms.النَّقْب: Al-Naqb (a place name marking a boundary)
key_terms.الْعَرِيض: Al-Areedh (a place name marking a boundary)
key_terms.ذُبَاب: Dhubab (a place name marking a boundary)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific geographical boundaries of the Haram of Medina according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* delineates the precise geographical boundaries of Medina’s *Haram*, establishing the sanctity of the space between Dhubab and Al-Naqb. The inclusion of variant markers like As-Sur and Ath-Thaniyyah reflects the scholarly tradition of reconciling multiple chains of transmission to define the extent of the Prophet’s sanctuary. These boundaries are not merely physical but carry legal implications for pilgrimage rites and the prohibition of hunting within the sacred precinct.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	With this chain of narrators, from Hussain Sa’eed, from Muhammed bin Sinan, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, declared as forbidden, from Medina, that which is from Dhubab Waqim, ‘Areedh and Naqb from the side of Mecca. Ibn Maskan said in his narration: And in another narration: From the two trumpets until the narrow mountain pass.
